sections.h2: Where does a Mecosta County deed get mailed or dropped off?
sections.html:
Recording packages are accepted by mail or courier at 400 Elm Street, Big Rapids, MI 49307, and the county page names USPS, UPS and FedEx as options. The phone is (231) 592-0148. Call first to learn the counter's recording hours.

The register maintains the real estate record for every parcel in Mecosta County. Indexing is complete back to January 1, 1968, and every document back to 1859 has been scanned and tagged by liber and page. Index books, including oil and gas, are imaged on the Countyfusion site, and a second public search runs through Vanguard at mecosta.mi.publicsearch.us.

The same office accepts passport applications for its own set of hours and a separate acceptance charge of $35. That service has no connection to a home sale.

sections.h2: What is Mecosta County like for a seller?
sections.html:
The county spreads over 571 square miles, 555 of them dry land, and holds more than 100 lakes, rivers and streams. The Muskegon River passes through Big Rapids, the county seat and largest city, where Ferris State University is located. County government was organized in 1859. Local government today includes 16 townships, the city of Big Rapids and four villages: Barryton, Mecosta, Morley and Stanwood.

Federal estimates count 42,320 people in mid-2025, a 4.9 percent gain on the 2020 base, spread over 21,490 housing units. The 2020 to 2024 survey found owners living in 76.9 percent of homes and pegged a typical house at $178,900, lower than in Marquette or Mason County.

Wherever the parcel sits, the deed is filed in Big Rapids, while assessing and collection stay with the township, village or city. Work out which local unit covers the parcel before asking for a payoff or tax certificate.

Schools are served by the Mecosta-Osceola Intermediate School District, based in Big Rapids, and the county has a charter school, Crossroads Charter Academy, along with Brockway Christian Academy, St. Michael Elementary and St. Peters Lutheran School.

sections.h2: What does the Mecosta County Register of Deeds charge for recording and copies?
sections.html:
Recording a deed, mortgage, lis pendens, affidavit or similar instrument costs $30.00 here. The county explains that the amount includes the statutory fee under MCL 600.2567a plus a $5.00 contribution to the automation fund. A document releasing several instruments adds $3.00 for each extra one.

Mecosta County Register of Deeds price list, copied from the county's fee section
ItemPrice
Deed or mortgage recording$30.00
Tax certificate with a warranty deed, up to five descriptions$5.00 per instrument
Each description beyond five$0.20
Copy of a land record, each page$1.00
Copy of a plat, each page$2.00
Name search$0.50 per year, $5.00 minimum
Certifying a record copy$5.00

The office also records fixture filings, timber to be cut and as-extracted collateral under the Uniform Commercial Code. All other personal property filings belong with the Secretary of State.

sections.h2: How is transfer tax worked out on a Mecosta County sale?
sections.html:
Two levies add together here. Mecosta County charges 55 cents per $500 slice of value and the state charges $3.75 per slice (MCL 207.525), with any partial slice counted as whole. A deed valued at $100 or more is taxable, and MCL 207.523 puts the liability on the grantor.

Take a $175,000 house: 350 slices, $1,312.50 to the state and $192.50 to the county, $1,505.00 combined. The Register of Deeds office collects both amounts alongside the recording fee, and the act calls for payment inside 15 days of delivering the deed.

The deed has to carry the property's full value. Alternatively, attach a valuation affidavit and add a line on the deed saying it is on file, which costs nothing to file. Claim any MCL 207.526 exemption on the deed's face, for instance for a parent-to-child transfer or a deed in lieu of foreclosure.

sections.h2: What makes the Mecosta County Register of Deeds reject a document?
sections.html:
An eleven-point checklist on the county page, drawn from Michigan statutes, governs what gets filed. These are the points that most often cause trouble:

  • Names printed under the signatures that differ from the notary acknowledgment
  • A missing grantee address, or no name and address for the drafter
  • A notary block with no commission expiration date
  • A deed naming a surviving owner without a certified death certificate on record
  • A court order lacking the clerk's certification and seal
  • Type under 10 point, or less than 2 1/2 inches of clear top margin
  • An opening line naming more than one recordable event
  • No statement of total property value and no affidavit

Stock should be white and 20-pound, from letter to legal size. Run through the list before mailing, since a rejected package costs days.

sections.h2: Does a Mecosta County deed need a tax certificate?
sections.html:
A warranty deed, a deed with a covenant of warranty, a land contract and an assignment of a land contract all do. The certificate comes from the county treasurer and shows taxes paid for the five years before the instrument date, under MCL 211.135. A quitclaim without warranty is excused.

The county treasurer's page describes how unpaid taxes move toward forfeiture and foreclosure, so a seller carrying old bills should ask for a payoff figure before closing. Mecosta County's companion property tax guide covers the summer and winter due dates, the March 1 delinquency date and the appeal calendar.

sections.h2: What do UCC filings and lien searches cost at the Mecosta County office?
sections.html:
The register records only the real-estate side of Uniform Commercial Code work: fixture filings, timber to be cut and as-extracted collateral. A standard-form filing with two debtor names and up to 100 pages is $30.00. Extra charges apply for a non-standard form ($7.00), for filings over 100 pages ($12.00) and for each debtor name past two ($10.00).

  • UCC search, per name: $6.00
  • State or federal tax lien certificate, per name: $3.00
  • Copy of a UCC filing, per page: $2.00
  • Copy of a state or federal tax lien, per page: $1.00

The county notes that its UCC search results cover personal property filings only through June 30, 2001. Real estate filings made after July 1, 2001 appear in the real estate index. Searches are done as time allows and carry no guarantee.

sections.h2: How old are the land records in Big Rapids and the surrounding villages?
sections.html:
The county was set off in 1840 and organized in 1859. The plat of the Village of Big Rapids was recorded on November 3, 1859, and French's addition (Glen Elm) followed on May 9, 1860. The state legislature authorized the City of Big Rapids in April 1869.

Railroads shaped the villages. The Grand Rapids and Indiana line crossed the Little Muskegon River in June 1869, creating the Village of Morley, and construction of the next stretch in late July 1869 brought the Village of Stanwood into existence. The register's documents back to 1859 are imaged, which helps when an old lot line or easement turns up in a title search.

sections.h2: Where can I look up Mecosta County parcels and maps?
sections.html:
The Equalization page links a land records portal and a map viewer, and it carries tax maps for each of the 16 townships: Aetna, Austin, Big Rapids, Chippewa, Colfax, Deerfield, Fork, Grant, Green, Hinton, Martiny, Mecosta, Millbrook, Morton, Sheridan and Wheatland. Its document center also lists the millage rates and a property tax estimator.

Lining up the parcel number on a tax map with the legal description on the deed is a quick way to catch a wrong lot before closing. The Vanguard support line, listed on the register's page, is (888) 608-1808.

faqs.q: What is Mecosta County's charge for filing a deed?
faqs.a: Thirty dollars per instrument, plus $3.00 for each additional instrument released in the same paper. Page copies are $1.00 each.

faqs.q: What would a $175,000 Mecosta County sale owe in transfer tax?
faqs.a: $1,505.00 in total, split into $1,312.50 for the state and $192.50 for the county. The seller carries it unless an exemption is stated on the deed.

faqs.q: What address takes Mecosta County recording packages?
faqs.a: 400 Elm Street, Big Rapids, MI 49307. Phone (231) 592-0148 beforehand to confirm paperwork and payment.

faqs.q: Is an uncertified court order good enough for Mecosta County recording?
faqs.a: No. The clerk of the court must certify and seal it. A plain copy is sent back.

faqs.q: How old are the Mecosta County records that can be searched?
faqs.a: The full index starts January 1, 1968, and papers from 1859 onward are scanned and tagged by liber and page. Countyfusion and Vanguard are the two public portals.
